research_questions.primary_outcome: percent change in body weight from baseline at week 52
research_questions.treatment_description: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide 15 mg plus lifestyle intervention for 52 weeks (n=71 randomized)
research_questions.control_description: Once-weekly subcutaneous placebo plus lifestyle intervention for 52 weeks (n=69 randomized)
research_questions.result_section_hint: Abstract, Results; Main Outcomes and Measures
research_questions.evidence_quote: The mean change in body weight at week 52 was −13.6% (95% CI, −15.8% to −11.4%) with tirzepatide 10 mg, −17.5% (95% CI, −19.7% to −15.3%) with tirzepatide 15 mg, and −2.3% with placebo (difference between 10 mg and placebo, −11.3% [95% CI, −14.3% to −8.3%; P < .001]; difference between 15 mg and placebo, −15.1% [95% CI, −18.2% to −12.1%; P < .001]).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide 15 mg < placebo (MD −15.1 percentage points; greater weight loss with tirzepatide)

content_sections.key_content_summary: States the clinical question and summarizes that mean percentage body-weight change at week 52 was −13.6% with tirzepatide 10 mg and −17.5% with tirzepatide 15 mg versus −2.3% with placebo, with statistically significant between-group differences.

content_sections.section_title: Importance; Objective; Design, Setting, and Participants; Interventions; Main Outcomes and Measures; Results; Conclusions and Relevance; Trial Registration
content_sections.key_content_summary: Structured abstract describes the phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 52-week trial in 210 Chinese adults and reports the co-primary percentage body-weight-change endpoint. Both tirzepatide doses produced significantly greater percentage weight reduction than placebo; the abstract also summarizes the categorical ≥5% weight-loss endpoint and safety.
Provides publication and correction information, author contributions, disclosures, sponsor role, and acknowledgments.
Briefly identifies the report as a randomized clinical trial of once-weekly tirzepatide for weight reduction in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes over 52 weeks.

research_questions.primary_outcome: Percent change in weight from baseline to week 72
research_questions.treatment_description: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide 15 mg plus lifestyle intervention for 72 weeks (n=311)
research_questions.control_description: Once-weekly matching placebo plus lifestyle intervention for 72 weeks (n=315)
research_questions.result_section_hint: Results, subsection “Change in body weight”; Table 2, co-primary endpoints at week 72
research_questions.evidence_quote: Both tirzepatide doses were superior to placebo, with estimated treatment differences relative to placebo of -9·6 percentage points (95% CI -11·1 to -8·1, p<0·0001) for the 10 mg dose and -11·6 percentage points (95% CI -13·0 to -10·1, p<0·0001) for the 15 mg dose (Table 2).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide 15 mg < placebo by -11.6 percentage points in body-weight change (favours tirzepatide)

content_sections.key_content_summary: Summarizes the phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trial in 938 adults with obesity/overweight and type 2 diabetes. At week 72, tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg produced greater percentage body-weight reductions than placebo, with estimated treatment differences of -9.6 and -11.6 percentage points, respectively.

Reviews prior obesity pharmacotherapy evidence in type 2 diabetes, explains the added value of SURMOUNT-2, and describes implications. It reports comparative weight-loss percentages from prior trials and summarizes the present trial's 72-week weight and metabolic findings.

Establishes obesity and weight management as major clinical priorities in type 2 diabetes, introduces tirzepatide as a dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, and states the objective of evaluating its efficacy and safety for chronic weight management.

Describes the 72-week multicentre double-blind parallel-group trial, randomization to weekly tirzepatide 10 mg, 15 mg, or placebo plus lifestyle intervention, outcomes, and statistical methods. Percentage change in body weight and achievement of at least 5% weight reduction at week 72 were co-primary endpoints; the treatment-regimen ANCOVA was the main regulatory analysis.

Reports participant flow, baseline characteristics, efficacy, cardiometabolic outcomes, quality of life, and safety. For the synthesis outcome, week-72 mean percentage weight changes were -12.8% for tirzepatide 10 mg, -14.7% for 15 mg, and -3.2% for placebo; both dose-specific adjusted contrasts favored tirzepatide.

Interprets the substantial 72-week body-weight reductions and accompanying glycaemic and cardiometabolic improvements, compares results with other tirzepatide and GLP-1 trials, discusses possible mechanisms and safety, and outlines strengths and limitations. The section includes the paper's conclusion that weekly tirzepatide produced clinically meaningful weight loss in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes.
Acknowledges Eli Lilly and Company funding and assistance with study design and medical writing.
Lists author roles in study design, trial conduct, data collection, statistical analysis, interpretation, and manuscript preparation.
Discloses investigator relationships with pharmaceutical and healthcare organizations and identifies several authors as Eli Lilly employees and shareholders.
Explains conditions and timing for requesting anonymized participant-level data and trial documents through a secure data-sharing environment.
Lists cited literature and regulatory guidance supporting the study background, design, and interpretation.

research_questions.primary_outcome: per cent change in body weight from randomization to week 72
research_questions.treatment_description: Tirzepatide maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) administered once weekly for 72 weeks after a 12-week intensive lifestyle intervention lead-in
research_questions.control_description: Matched placebo administered once weekly for 72 weeks after the same 12-week intensive lifestyle intervention lead-in
research_questions.result_section_hint: Results > Primary outcomes; Figure 'Effect of once-weekly tirzepatide on body weight in comparison with placebo'; Table 'Efficacy findings from randomization (week 0) to week 72'
research_questions.evidence_quote: For the treatment regimen estimand (TRE) the mean change at week 72 was −18.4% (s.e. 0.7) with tirzepatide MTD and 2.5% (s.e. 1.0) with placebo. Tirzepatide MTD was superior to placebo, with an estimated treatment difference relative to placebo of −20.8 percentage points (95% CI −23.2, −18.5; < 0.001).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide < placebo (greater weight loss with tirzepatide; favors tirzepatide)

content_sections.key_content_summary: Summarizes the randomized, double-blind comparison of once-weekly tirzepatide maximum tolerated dose versus placebo for 72 weeks after an intensive lifestyle lead-in. Both coprimary endpoints were met, including a −20.8 percentage-point treatment difference in body-weight change favoring tirzepatide.

Reviews obesity-related risks, limitations of lifestyle intervention, and evidence for incretin-based antiobesity drugs. States that the trial evaluated tirzepatide efficacy 72 weeks after randomization among adults who had lost at least 5% of baseline weight during a 12-week intensive lifestyle lead-in.

Reports participant disposition, baseline characteristics, efficacy, and safety. For the primary treatment-regimen estimand, mean percentage body-weight change from randomization to week 72 was −18.4% with tirzepatide and 2.5% with placebo, an adjusted difference of −20.8 percentage points (95% CI −23.2 to −18.5; P<0.001).

Interprets tirzepatide as producing substantial additional weight loss after successful intensive lifestyle intervention and discusses clinical implications, comparisons with other antiobesity therapies, safety, strengths, and limitations. Concludes that tirzepatide produced clinically meaningful additional body-weight reduction.

Describes the 84-week multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled design, eligibility criteria, 12-week lifestyle lead-in, randomization, treatment procedures, outcomes, and statistical analysis. Percentage change in body weight from randomization to week 72 was a coprimary endpoint analyzed under treatment-regimen and efficacy estimands.

Provides links to the reporting summary, source data, extended data, supplementary information, acknowledgements, peer review materials, author contributions, competing interests, and data/code availability.
Lists supplementary materials, including investigators, protocol, statistical analysis plan, and reporting summary.
Contains supplementary figures and tables on body weight over time, blood pressure, gastrointestinal adverse events, study design, participant demographics, and additional efficacy findings.

research_questions.primary_outcome: Percent change in body weight at week 52
research_questions.treatment_description: Maximum tolerated dose of tirzepatide (10 mg or 15 mg) subcutaneously once weekly for 52 weeks plus lifestyle counseling
research_questions.control_description: Placebo subcutaneously once weekly for 52 weeks plus lifestyle counseling
research_questions.result_section_hint: Change in PROs and Cardiovascular Risk Factors; Table 2, key secondary end points
research_questions.evidence_quote: Participants in both trials who received tirzepatide had significant reductions in body weight (Figs. 1C and 1D), systolic blood pressure, and hsCRP concentrations (Table 2).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide < placebo (estimated treatment difference −16.1 percentage points, 95% CI −18.0 to −14.2; favors tirzepatide)

research_questions.primary_outcome: Percent change in body weight at week 52
research_questions.treatment_description: Maximum tolerated dose of tirzepatide (10 mg or 15 mg) subcutaneously once weekly for 52 weeks, with continued PAP therapy and lifestyle counseling
research_questions.control_description: Placebo subcutaneously once weekly for 52 weeks, with continued PAP therapy and lifestyle counseling
research_questions.result_section_hint: Change in PROs and Cardiovascular Risk Factors; Table 2, key secondary end points
research_questions.evidence_quote: Participants in both trials who received tirzepatide had significant reductions in body weight (Figs. 1C and 1D), systolic blood pressure, and hsCRP concentrations (Table 2).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide < placebo (estimated treatment difference −17.3 percentage points, 95% CI −19.3 to −15.3; favors tirzepatide)

content_sections.key_content_summary: Summarizes two 52-week randomized placebo-controlled SURMOUNT-OSA trials. Tirzepatide significantly reduced AHI and improved all prespecified key secondary outcomes, including percentage body-weight change, versus placebo.

Describes obstructive sleep apnea, limitations of mechanical therapies, obesity as a reversible etiologic factor, and the rationale for testing the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide in adults with obesity and sleep apnea.
Describes two 52-week phase 3 multicenter, parallel-group, double-blind randomized trials: Trial 1 enrolled participants not using PAP, and Trial 2 enrolled participants using PAP.

Defines eligibility as adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity and lists key exclusions, including diabetes, recent major weight change, and planned sleep-apnea or obesity surgery.
Details 1:1 assignment to once-weekly tirzepatide or placebo, dose escalation to a maximum tolerated 10 mg or 15 mg dose, common lifestyle counseling, masking, and polysomnography assessments.

Defines change in AHI as the primary endpoint and percentage change in body weight as a multiplicity-controlled key secondary endpoint assessed from baseline to week 52, alongside other sleep and cardiovascular-risk outcomes.

Describes power calculations, treatment-regimen and efficacy estimands, multiplicity control, ANCOVA and logistic-regression models, and multiple-imputation procedures. The treatment-regimen estimand is the default reported analysis.
Reports randomization of 469 participants across Trial 1 (N=234) and Trial 2 (N=235), completion and adherence, and demographic and clinical baseline characteristics.
Reports significant reductions in AHI and hypoxic burden with tirzepatide versus placebo in both trials, along with categorical AHI response outcomes.

content_sections.section_title: ## Change in PROs and Cardiovascular Risk Factors
content_sections.key_content_summary: Reports significant reductions with tirzepatide in body weight in both trials and in pooled sleep-related patient-reported outcomes, systolic blood pressure, and hsCRP. Table 2 provides the eligible week-52 percentage body-weight contrasts.
Reports adverse events, serious adverse events, discontinuations, and events of special interest; gastrointestinal events were most frequent with tirzepatide and no deaths occurred.

Interprets clinically meaningful improvements in sleep-disordered breathing, sleep-related functioning, body weight, blood pressure, and inflammation, discusses safety and generalizability, and notes limitations including 52-week duration and lack of long-term cardiovascular outcomes.
Bibliography supporting the clinical background, trial methods, outcome measures, and interpretation.

research_questions.target_construct: percentage body weight change from baseline
research_questions.primary_outcome: Percent change at 52 weeks in body weight
research_questions.treatment_description: Tirzepatide, initiated at 2.5 mg subcutaneously once weekly and escalated every 4 weeks as tolerated to a maximum of 15 mg once weekly, in addition to usual therapy
research_questions.control_description: Matching placebo subcutaneously once weekly, in addition to usual therapy
research_questions.result_section_hint: Results — Key Secondary End Points; Table 2
research_questions.evidence_quote: At 52 weeks, the mean percent change in body weight was −13.9% in the tirzepatide group and −2.2% in the placebo group (between-group difference, −11.6 percentage points; 95% CI, −12.9 to −10.4; P<0.001).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide < placebo (greater percentage weight loss with tirzepatide; favors tirzepatide)

content_sections.key_content_summary: Summarizes the randomized placebo-controlled SUMMIT trial. Tirzepatide reduced the cardiovascular-death/worsening-heart-failure composite, improved KCCQ-CSS, and produced more treatment discontinuations due to adverse events than placebo.

content_sections.section_title: Unheaded introduction (beginning “T failure and a preserved ejection fraction…”)
content_sections.key_content_summary: Explains the links among obesity, inflammation, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, reviews semaglutide evidence, and motivates testing tirzepatide for heart-failure outcomes, health status, and functional capacity.

Describes the international double-blind randomized trial of 731 adults with obesity and HFpEF assigned to once-weekly tirzepatide up to 15 mg or placebo. Specifies dual primary endpoints, key secondary endpoints including percent change in body weight at 52 weeks, and intention-to-treat statistical methods.

Reports participant disposition, dual primary outcomes, key secondary outcomes, and safety. At 52 weeks, mean percentage body-weight change was −13.9% with tirzepatide and −2.2% with placebo, an adjusted between-group difference of −11.6 percentage points (95% CI −12.9 to −10.4; P<0.001).

Interprets tirzepatide as reducing major heart-failure events and improving health status and exercise tolerance while decreasing body weight and inflammation. Discusses possible mechanisms, safety, generalizability, and the BMI-based eligibility limitation.
Lists cited literature on obesity, HFpEF, incretin therapies, inflammation, and cardiovascular outcomes.

research_questions.primary_outcome: Percent change in bodyweight from baseline to week 72
research_questions.treatment_description: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide 15 mg, dose-escalated from 2.5 mg, plus lifestyle intervention for 72 weeks
research_questions.control_description: Once-weekly subcutaneous placebo plus the same lifestyle intervention for 72 weeks
research_questions.evidence_quote: At week 72, the least-squares mean percent change from baseline in bodyweight was −17·8%, −22·7%, and −1·7% in the tirzepatide 10-mg, tirzepatide 15-mg, and placebo groups, respectively, with estimated treatment diferences (ETDs) relative to placebo of −16·1% (95% CI −18·7 to −13·5; p<0·0001) and −21·1% (95% CI −23·6 to −18·5; p<0·0001) in the 10-mg and 15-mg groups, respectively (table 2).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide 15 mg < placebo (greater percentage body-weight reduction; ETD −21.1 percentage points)

content_sections.key_content_summary: Structured summary of the SURMOUNT-J randomized trial. At week 72, tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg produced placebo-adjusted body-weight changes of −16.1 and −21.1 percentage points, respectively; categorical weight-loss and safety findings are also summarized.

Describes obesity disease definitions and risks in Japan, the rationale for pharmacotherapy, prior SURMOUNT findings, and the objective of evaluating tirzepatide versus placebo for chronic weight management in Japanese adults.
Places SURMOUNT-J in the context of prior semaglutide and tirzepatide trials in global and east Asian populations and summarizes the study's added value and clinical implications.
Summarizes the literature search and prior weight-loss evidence for semaglutide and tirzepatide, including SURMOUNT and east Asian studies.

States that tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg achieved clinically meaningful weight reduction and improved cardiometabolic and body-composition measures versus placebo in Japanese adults with obesity disease.

content_sections.section_title: ## Implications of all the available evidence
content_sections.key_content_summary: Explains the therapeutic relevance of the observed weight reduction and improvement in obesity-related health disorders and identifies both tirzepatide doses as potential treatment options.
Umbrella methods section covering trial design, eligibility, randomization, intervention, outcomes, statistical analysis, and sponsor role.
Describes the multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled 72-week phase 3 design, Japanese eligibility criteria, excluded diabetes, and exclusion of one site for regulatory noncompliance.
Participants were assigned 1:1:1 to tirzepatide 10 mg, tirzepatide 15 mg, or placebo, with stratified central randomization and masking of participants, investigators, site staff, and sponsor.
Details dose escalation from 2.5 mg to assigned dose, weekly injections, common lifestyle counseling, prohibited weight-management medications, and centralized imaging and laboratory assessments.

Defines coprimary endpoints as percent change in bodyweight and achievement of at least 5% weight reduction at week 72, plus secondary metabolic, body-composition, patient-reported, exploratory, and safety outcomes.

Specifies mITT and efficacy-estimand analyses, MMRM for percent body-weight change, logistic regression for categorical outcomes, multiplicity handling, missing-data methods, and supplementary treatment-regimen analyses.
Reports sponsor involvement in design, data collection and analysis, interpretation, manuscript preparation, and publication decision.

Reports participant flow, baseline data, efficacy, and safety. The primary efficacy-estimand analysis found week-72 placebo-adjusted percent body-weight changes of −16.1 points for 10 mg and −21.1 points for 15 mg, both p<0.0001.

content_sections.section_title: ## Figure 2: Efect of tirzepatide on bodyweight and obesity-related health disorders
content_sections.key_content_summary: Figure legend describes longitudinal mean percent body-weight change, categorical weight-loss targets, and improvement in obesity-related health disorders, including analysis and imputation methods.

Interprets clinically meaningful weight reduction and improvements in metabolic and body-composition measures, compares findings with prior SURMOUNT trials, reviews safety, and discusses strengths, limitations, and generalizability.
States author contributions, guarantor responsibilities, statistical-analysis responsibility, and manuscript approval.
Discloses industry funding, grants, consulting, honoraria, employment, and stock ownership.
Describes conditions, timing, review, and secure-environment procedures for requesting anonymized participant data and trial documents.
Acknowledges participants, families, project management, and sponsor-funded medical writing and editing.
Bibliography supporting the trial background, methods, and discussion.

research_questions.primary_outcome: Change in body weight from week 36 to 88, %
research_questions.treatment_description: Continued once-weekly subcutaneous maximum tolerated dose of tirzepatide (10 or 15 mg) for 52 weeks after the 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in (n=335 randomized).
research_questions.control_description: Switched to once-weekly matching placebo for 52 weeks after the 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in (n=335 randomized).
research_questions.result_section_hint: Results, Double-Blind Period, Primary End Point; Table 2
research_questions.evidence_quote: For the treatment regimen estimand, the mean percent change in weight from week 36 to week 88 was −5.5% with tirzepatide vs 14.0% with placebo (difference, −19.4% [95% CI, −21.2% to −17.7%]; P < .001; Table 2; eFigure 2A in Supplement 2).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide < placebo; MD −19.4 percentage points, favoring tirzepatide

content_sections.key_content_summary: Summarizes the randomized-withdrawal SURMOUNT-4 trial. From week 36 to 88, continued tirzepatide produced a mean weight change of −5.5% versus +14.0% after switching to placebo, an adjusted difference of −19.4 percentage points (95% CI, −21.2 to −17.7; P<.001).

Describes obesity as a chronic relapsing condition, reviews evidence of weight regain after stopping antiobesity medication, and explains tirzepatide's GIP/GLP-1 activity. States the trial aim of comparing continued maximum-tolerated-dose tirzepatide with placebo for maintenance of weight reduction.

Details the 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in followed by 52 weeks of randomized double-blind continued tirzepatide (10 or 15 mg weekly) versus matching placebo in 670 adults. Defines percent change in body weight from week 36 to 88 as the primary endpoint and specifies ANCOVA for the treatment-regimen estimand and a repeated-measures mixed model for the efficacy estimand.

Reports participant flow, baseline characteristics, efficacy, and safety. For the primary treatment-regimen estimand, percent body-weight change from randomization at week 36 to week 88 was −5.5% with continued tirzepatide and +14.0% with placebo, for a difference of −19.4 percentage points (95% CI, −21.2 to −17.7; P<.001).

Interprets the randomized-withdrawal findings as evidence that ongoing pharmacotherapy is needed to prevent weight regain and preserve cardiometabolic benefits. Notes that participants switched to placebo retained some net loss from initial enrollment but regained substantial weight after randomization.

Concludes that, after initial weight reduction during the tirzepatide lead-in, continued maximum-tolerated-dose tirzepatide yielded superior weight maintenance and further reduction compared with switching to placebo.

Frames the clinical question and summarizes that participants switched to placebo regained 14% from randomization while those continuing tirzepatide lost an additional 5.5% during the 52-week double-blind period.

Notes that postrandomization dose adjustment was not permitted, intensive behavioral therapy was not evaluated, and randomized participants represented those who tolerated the 10- or 15-mg lead-in regimen.
Provides publication details, author affiliations and contributions, conflicts of interest, funding and sponsor roles, presentation history, data-sharing information, and acknowledgments.
Lists cited literature on obesity management, weight maintenance, tirzepatide, and other antiobesity therapies.

research_questions.primary_outcome: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 72
research_questions.treatment_description: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide 15 mg plus lifestyle intervention for 72 weeks (n=630); the highest dose is selected because no pooled tirzepatide-versus-placebo estimate was reported and the synthesis plan specifies using 15 mg when only dose-specific contrasts are available.
research_questions.control_description: Once-weekly matching placebo plus lifestyle intervention for 72 weeks (n=643).
research_questions.result_section_hint: Section 'Change in Body Weight', Figure 1A, and Table 2
research_questions.evidence_quote: All three tirzepatide doses were superior to placebo, with estimated treatment differences relative to placebo of −11.9 percentage points (95% CI, −13.4 to −10.4) for the 5-mg dose, −16.4 percentage points (95% CI, −17.9 to −14.8) for the 10-mg dose, and −17.8 percentage points (95% CI, −19.3 to −16.3) for the 15-mg dose (P<0.001 for all comparisons).
research_questions.effect_direction: tirzepatide 15 mg < placebo by −17.8 percentage points in percentage body-weight change (favours tirzepatide)

content_sections.key_content_summary: Summarizes the phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled SURMOUNT-1 trial in 2539 adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes. Tirzepatide 5, 10, and 15 mg produced significantly greater percentage body-weight reductions at week 72 than placebo, with gastrointestinal adverse events most common.

Describes obesity burden, limitations of lifestyle treatment, incretin-based pharmacotherapy, and the rationale for dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonism. Introduces SURMOUNT-1 as an evaluation of tirzepatide efficacy and safety in adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes.
Introduces the trial methods, detailed in the following trial-design, participant, procedure, endpoint, and statistical-analysis subsections.
Describes the multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial conducted at 119 sites in nine countries, including oversight, ethics, and sponsor roles.
Defines adult eligibility by BMI and weight-related complications and lists key exclusions, including diabetes, recent major weight change, obesity surgery, and recent weight-loss medication.

Participants were randomized 1:1:1:1 to weekly tirzepatide 5, 10, or 15 mg or matching placebo for 72 weeks, all with lifestyle intervention; tirzepatide was escalated from 2.5 mg over up to 20 weeks.

Defines coprimary endpoints as percentage change in body weight and achievement of at least 5% weight reduction at week 72. Lists key secondary cardiometabolic, physical-function, body-composition, and safety assessments.

Reports power assumptions and intention-to-treat analysis using treatment-regimen and efficacy estimands. The treatment-regimen estimand was primary in the report and assessed effects regardless of discontinuation; multiplicity was controlled for coprimary and key secondary endpoints.
Introduces participant flow, body-weight efficacy, cardiometabolic, body-composition, and safety results detailed in subsequent subsections.
Reports enrollment of 2539 participants, completion and adherence rates, treatment discontinuations, and baseline demographic and clinical characteristics.

At week 72, treatment-regimen estimates for percentage body-weight change were −15.0%, −19.5%, and −20.9% for tirzepatide 5, 10, and 15 mg versus −3.1% for placebo. Dose-specific placebo-adjusted differences were −11.9, −16.4, and −17.8 percentage points, respectively, all P<0.001.

content_sections.section_title: ## Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Physical Function
content_sections.key_content_summary: Reports improvements with tirzepatide in waist circumference, blood pressure, insulin, lipids, prediabetes status, and SF-36 physical function compared with placebo.
In the dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry subgroup, tirzepatide produced greater reduction in total fat mass and improved the fat-to-lean-mass ratio compared with placebo.
Reports overall and serious adverse events, deaths, gastrointestinal events, pancreatitis, gallbladder events, and other adverse events of interest across tirzepatide doses and placebo.

Interprets the substantial and sustained weight loss with tirzepatide, compares the magnitude contextually with other obesity therapies, reviews cardiometabolic and safety findings, and discusses strengths and limitations. Concludes that all three weekly tirzepatide doses reduced weight in adults with obesity.
Lists the literature cited for obesity epidemiology, treatment guidance, incretin biology, prior pharmacotherapy trials, statistical guidance, and adverse-event context.
